clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive sensory and autonomic neuropathy that is essentially confined to individuals of Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry through a founder mutation
Caused by mutations in ELP1 (formerly IKBKAP) affecting a subunit of the Elongator complex
Autonomic crises are characteristic, with paroxysmal hypertension, tachycardia, sweating, blotching, cyclical vomiting and marked emotional lability
Cardinal signs include absent fungiform papillae on the tongue, absent overflow tears (alacrima), depressed reflexes and reduced pain and temperature sensation
Cardiovascular instability with orthostatic hypotension yet paroxysmal hypertension reflects the baroreflex failure at the core of the disease
Recurrent aspiration from swallowing incoordination and impaired airway protection is a major source of morbidity
The absence of an axon flare after intradermal histamine and characteristic autonomic findings support the diagnosis, confirmed by ELP1 testing
Management is supportive and multidisciplinary, including fludrocortisone or other measures for blood-pressure instability, aggressive treatment of crises, and aspiration prevention
reference.pathophysiology: Familial dysautonomia is caused by biallelic mutation in ELP1 (IKBKAP), which encodes a scaffold subunit of the Elongator complex involved in transfer-RNA modification and gene transcription. The predominant Ashkenazi founder variant reduces functional ELP1 in a tissue-specific manner, impairing development and survival of sensory and autonomic neurons. This leads to progressive depletion of neurons in the dorsal root and autonomic ganglia, producing baroreflex failure, defective control of blood pressure, temperature and secretions, reduced pain and temperature sensation, and impaired airway protection. The autonomic crises reflect unbuffered sympathetic surges from this baroreflex and afferent failure.
additionalDifferentials: Congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis (HSAN4)
Mitochondrial disorders with autonomic and sensory involvement
Acquired autonomic neuropathies (e.g. autoimmune autonomic ganglionopathy)
Gastro-oesophageal reflux and cyclical vomiting syndromes of other cause
additionalInvestigations: Targeted ELP1 (IKBKAP) genetic testing, including the founder mutation
Autonomic function and tilt-table testing to characterise baroreflex failure
Assessment for absent fungiform papillae and absent overflow tears
Intradermal histamine test showing an absent axon flare
Swallowing and aspiration assessment (video fluoroscopy) given aspiration risk
Nerve conduction and sensory testing to document the sensory neuropathy
redFlags: Severe autonomic (dysautonomic) crisis with dangerous hypertension, tachycardia and vomiting
Aspiration pneumonia or acute airway compromise
Profound orthostatic hypotension causing syncope and falls
Cardiac arrhythmia or sudden unexpected death associated with autonomic instability
reference.prognosis: Survival has improved with specialist multidisciplinary care, though morbidity and mortality remain substantial from aspiration, cardiovascular instability, autonomic crises and sudden death. Progressive optic neuropathy, worsening gait ataxia and renal impairment can develop over time.
pitfalls: Not recognising an autonomic crisis and thereby delaying urgent supportive treatment
Overlooking silent aspiration as a driver of recurrent respiratory illness
Missing the clinical clues of absent fungiform papillae and alacrima
Managing blood pressure without accounting for the combination of orthostatic hypotension and paroxysmal hypertension
references: Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: Multidisciplinary supportive care as the mainstay, since no disease-specific therapy exists
Aspiration prevention with swallowing assessment, texture-modified feeding or gastrostomy, and chest physiotherapy
Management of autonomic crises with benzodiazepines such as diazepam and with clonidine, alongside rehydration and antiemesis
Treat orthostatic hypotension with volume and salt repletion, fludrocortisone and midodrine while controlling paroxysmal hypertension
Ocular protection for alacrima with artificial tears and lubricants
Ongoing surveillance for cardiovascular instability, renal impairment, scoliosis and optic neuropathy
Genetic counselling with ELP1 testing and carrier screening in individuals of Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry
